newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says well spudded off Australia.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says well spudded off Australia.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday the first exploration well in Zoca block 95-18 off northern Australia, where Statoil has a 25 percent interest, was spudded last Saturday.
It said this well was being drilled in a gas prospect about 400 kilometres northwest of Darwin, in the Zone of Cooperation (Zoca) agreed by the Australian and Indonesian authorities.

"This is a high-risk prospect, where we hope to make such a large discovery that we can compete on delivering liquefied natural gas to Asian markets," Oddbjoerg Greiner, Australia project manager in International Exploration & Production, told Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter.

Mobil Corp, operator for the block with a 25 percent interest, has assigned responsibility for the first well to Royal Dutch/Shell, which also has 25 percent. The other partners are Hardy Oil & Gas Plc, with 13 percent, and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd with 12 percent, it said.
Being drilled by Ocean Epoch in about 200 metres of water, the well should take two to three months to complete, Status Weekly said.
